messages:
alex: FYI support escalation from Horizon — p99 shot up from ~180ms -> ~420ms around 20:07 UTC after the continuous-batcher change. Customer reports intermittent timeouts. dashboard: https://redwood.app/d/TEAM/continuous-batcher?panel=tail_latency :eyes:
support-lead: Thanks. Do we know which commit/deploy touched batcher config?
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-16_20:00 by jamal (rollout id r-20260316-77) changed continuous_batcher.hold_ms from 8 -> 2 for chat-serve-prod
jamal: That was me — experiment to lower avg latency for medium prompts. Didn't expect tail inflation.
priya: Can we get p95/p99 before/after?
alex: before (19:40-20:00): p95 95ms p99 180ms. after (20:10-20:30): p95 110ms p99 420ms. Request size skew: many tiny prompts (<16 tokens) increased.
alex: attaching quick log snip:
```
2026-03-16T20:07:12Z chat-serve-prod instance-5 batcher: batch formed size=3 hold_ms=2 emit_ms=20 tail_latency=380
2026-03-16T20:07:12Z chat-serve-prod instance-9 batcher: batch formed size=1 hold_ms=2 emit_ms=200 tail_latency=410
```
support-lead: So small single-request batches getting held briefly then queued — increased head-of-line blocking?
jamal: Looks like lowering hold_ms reduced average latency but increased variance when microbursts align with KV cache misses. Small batches are getting serialized across GPU warmup.
priya: Can we reproduce locally with a microburst script? If yes, get flame/trace.
alex: Repro steps I used (quick):
```
# spike 200 tiny requests over 2s
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
sleep 0.01
done
```
I see the same p99 directional increase when hold_ms <= 3.
ops-runner: Immediate mitigation: rolling config change to bump hold_ms back to 8 on chat-serve-prod canary 20:35 UTC. Command:
```
rdctl rollout set chat-serve-prod continuous_batcher.hold_ms=8 --rollout=canary
```
jamal: Doing that now.
deploy-bot: rollout started r-20260316-77f-fix at 20:36
jamal: canary looks good — p99 back to ~190ms in canary. Rolling to remainder.
ops-runner: Full rollout done 20:41. Observed tail drop to ~195ms overall by 20:45. :tada:
priya: Good quick mitigation. Long term we should avoid a single global small hold_ms; propose adaptive grace window based on recent prompt-size distribution + GPU warmup state.
support-lead: I'll update ticket #INC-4821 with mitigation and notify Horizon.
alex: Follow-ups:
- add canary checks in the batcher config change playbook (verify p99 for small prompts)
- add test harness for microburst scripts to PRs touching hold_ms
- consider defaulting to min_hold_ms=6 and an adaptive lower bound rather than 2
jamal: Agree. I'll open an RFC and include quantile smoke tests in CI.
priya: Also log per-batch size + latency in metrics pipeline for a week so we can tune thresholds.
ops-runner: Closing escalation after support confirms Horizon saw improved latency. Please add postmortem note when RFC lands.
support-lead: Confirmed with customer: they saw 50% fewer timeouts after rollback. Closing on our side. :white_check_mark:
alex: Thanks everyone. I'll start the RFC draft and link here.
